candidates.original_title: Evaluation of an enhanced stimulus-stimulus pairing procedure to increase early vocalizations of children with autism
candidates.description: The effect of an enhanced stimulus-stimulus pairing procedure on increasing vocalizations in children with autism
candidates.citation_sentence: The current study replicated an enhanced stimulus-stimulus pairing (SSP) procedure used by Esch et al. (Journal of Applied Behavior Analysis 42: 42-225, 2009) for increasing vocalizations in children with autism.
candidates.notes: Two of three participants showed substantial increases in target vocalizations; Paul showed minimal change. Authors explicitly state they replicated the procedure and support its efficacy, so result is success despite the mixed participant-level outcome. Mixed results across three participants: Mary and Aaron showed substantial increases in target vocalizations, but Paul showed minimal increase. Authors state 'The present study replicated' but the effect was not uniform across all participants, making the overall outcome ambiguous between success and inconclusive.
